title: Geometric input bounds for the package exchanges
statement: Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime. Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ form a Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and separated finite-type $k$-morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Every corner is Noetherian, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and finite-dimensional, every arrow is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $\ell$ is invertible on every corner. There exists $e\ge0$ such that every geometric fibre $X_{\bar y}$ of $f$ has topological Krull dimension at most $e$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; empty fibres have dimension $-\infty$. If $f$ is proper, then $f'$ is proper. Every separated finite-type morphism to any of these corners admits a compactification $U\xrightarrow{j}\overline U\xrightarrow{p}T$ with $j$ quasi-compact open, $p$ proper and $pj$ the given morphism [def-nagata-compactification].

source.place: Clause (4), base-change sentence; argument separated from realization steps 1,2.

proof.text: For each corner T, quasi-compactness follows from its quasi-compact structure morphism to the affine spectrum of k [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. A field is Noetherian, so LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes T locally Noetherian; combined with compactness this gives IsNoetherian T. Locally Noetherian schemes are quasi-separated. Apply [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] to the same structure morphism for a natural dimension bound. These arguments include empty corners.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; blueprint lem-kun-dimension-finite-type and Tag 01K4 for quasi-compactness

proof.text: Every arrow is quasi-compact by assumption and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Derive characteristic p of k_0 from its cardinality p^a, then transport characteristic through the injective algebra map to k. Since ell is prime and differs from p, its cast to k is nonzero and hence a unit. Map this unit through the composite k to Gamma(T,top) to the stalk at t. Ring homomorphisms preserve natural casts and units, yielding invertibility on every corner, vacuously on an empty corner.

source.place: Definition 01KK, paragraph following it, using Tag 01K7; scalar inverse pulled along the k-scheme structure

proof.text: By Step 1, $Y$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to the given finite-type morphism $f$ to choose one integer $e\ge0$ with $\dim X_y\le e$ for all points $y\in Y$. This is a bound for ordinary scheme fibres, not yet for geometric fibres.

For an arbitrary field-valued point ybar : Spec Omega to Y, use Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField to obtain its image point y and residue-field map kappa(y) to Omega. Its inverse equation factors ybar through Y.fromSpecResidueField y. The ordinary fibre Z=X_y is locally of finite type over kappa(y) by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. For nonempty Z, apply [lem-pc-dim-base-change-affine-covers] for the induced algebra structure to obtain matching covers U_i of Z and V_i of its scalar extension. Each dim U_i is at most dim Z and hence e by [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone]. Tensor-factor symmetry, homeomorphism invariance, and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension] give dim V_i = dim U_i. This works for every Omega, in particular every algebraically closed Omega.

source.place: Tag 00P3, lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension; matching affine charts as in Tags 01JR and 01JQ, finite type base change Tag 01T4

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-bound-open-cover] on the scalar extension, which is sober by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], to the bounds of Step 4. If Z is empty, the projection from its scalar extension makes that extension empty. An empty space has no irreducible closed subsets, so its dimension is bottom by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Finally pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso and the residue-field factorization identify the scalar extension with the given pullback X times_Y Spec Omega; its homeomorphism transports the bound. Separately the same irreducible-closed-subset argument proves that every empty geometric fibre has dimension bottom. The natural number e was chosen before ybar.

source.place: Tag 0B7I, lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions, open-cover bound; Tag 0055, definition-Krull, empty case

proof.text: If $f$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] applied along $g$ makes the projection $X\times_Y Y\prime\to Y\prime$ proper. The chosen Cartesian identification in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] identifies this projection with $f\prime$, so $f\prime$ is proper.

For any corner T and separated finite-type morphism h:U to T, Step 1 supplies a compact quasi-separated base. Use [thm-nagata-compactification] to obtain c=NagataCompactification h. Its open factor is quasi-compact by Compactification.quasiCompact_openImmersion [def-nagata-compactification] applied to the assumed QuasiCompact h; this is a consequence of quasi-compact cancellation against the separated proper factor, rather than a field built into Compactification.

source.place: Tag 0F41, theorem-nagata; blueprint thm-nagata-compactification and def-nagata-compactification
